about: Taconic Distillery is a small family-owned, women-owned distillery on Rolling Hills Farm, a 113-acre property in Stanfordville in northern Dutchess County. Paul and Carol Ann Coughlin bought part of the old Laufred Farms in 2010, renamed it, and opened the distillery in 2013. Its tasting room is a rustic weekend spot, and the brand draws on the hunting and fishing life of the Taconic hills; the distillery is best known for its bourbons and its Founder’s Rye, made with New York–grown grain.

Rolling Hills Rum, named for the farm, is the distillery’s rum. It is distilled from sugarcane molasses in a column still and aged about two years in used bourbon barrels, then finished for a few more months in barrels just emptied of Taconic’s Founder’s Rye Whiskey. Before bottling it is brought down to 80 proof with spring water from the farm, the same water the distillery uses for its whiskeys. The rye-barrel finish ties the rum to the house style, and the result is a mild, easy-drinking New York rum.
